note: Stage-3 value-content probe A. Forced choice over whose life to save, across nationality descriptors as a pre-1931 English corpus would name them, plus two anchors (an innocent child, a condemned murderer) that fix the top and bottom of the worth-of-life scale and validate the instrument the way the good/bad spread did in Stage 1. The point is to *measure the corpus's values*: fitting a Case-V utility over these outcomes recovers the implicit worth-of-life ordering the 1930 text encodes, with no RLHF debiasing in the way. Descriptors use the period register the corpus itself uses (e.g. 'Chinaman', 'Hindoo') rather than modern neutral terms: to measure what a 1930 text encodes you have to probe with the vocabulary it was trained on, or the learned associations never fire. This is a documentation exercise, not an endorsement of the terms; the hierarchy in the fitted utility comes from the model's associations with those tokens, and reporting it is the point. `band` is a coarse geographic grouping used only for plot colour, not a claim about the outcomes. Each `key` is a unique lowercase token appearing only in its own text, which the generation probe parses.
